title: An unchanged saturating oxygen-use law fits A20 oxygen and dual tracers in 2012 and 2021 with a 50-year age limit and 5% tolerance
abstract: We tested whether one unchanged oxygen-use law can fit GLODAPv2.2023 oxygen, CFC-12 and SF6 on sigma0 26.5 at A20 in 2012 and 2021. Linear programs optimize over all age spectra and the full continuous sets of common rate and preformed AOU. With a 50-year age limit and 5% tracer tolerance, a constant rate has a minimum maximum AOU error of 1.175 umol/kg across six paired latitude bins. An unchanged saturating law with a 10-year rate-decay time, zero preformed AOU and 88.780 umol/kg asymptotic oxygen use fits every bin in both years. All its components retain at least 143.588 umol/kg oxygen. At 2% tolerance no tested law fits A20 with nonnegative preformed AOU. A22 admits a constant-rate fit. A 200-year age limit permits a constant-rate A20 fit when the component-inventory restriction is removed. Thus the remaining constant-rate residual does not require a change in respiration. This is a compatibility test, not process attribution. Free spectra, fixed saturation, partial-pressure mixing, sparse occupations and uncertain oxygen levels limit the result. Code, aggregate results, provenance, dual checks and exact nonlinear witness audits are included; external records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Minimum maximum AOU error under common oxygen-use laws at 5% tracer tolerance. Zero gives an exact joint fit. The inventory rule is conservative.

citations.reason: We reuse its selection code and extend its finite rate grid to a continuous parameter test and saturating oxygen use.
A constant-rate residual does not require a change in the oxygen-use law in the tested broad spectrum model.
